subject: Limited forensic access & notice-window coordination for potential exposure
messages:
From: Joanna Li <joanna.li@acmehealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Potential data exposure — initial info request

Hi Vanessa,

We detected unusual activity that may have touched a small subset of user records in our environment. At this stage it looks limited, but the legal and security teams have asked for a quick alignment on notification timelines and evidence handover to satisfy our DPA obligations. Can you confirm the following as quickly as possible: 

- Redwood's standard acknowledgment window for an inbound incident notification from a customer (we need this for our internal escalation matrix).
- The narrowest scope of data you can provide as an export for forensic review (e.g., identifiers only, hashed PII, request/response logs excluding full user content).
- Whether Redwood can provide a time-limited, encrypted forensic snapshot (read-only) to an Acme-controlled SFTP or whether you require shared custody with a third-party subprocessor for the export.
- Which subprocessors would be engaged if an evidence export is performed (we're concerned about cross-border subprocessors and want to avoid additional approvals).

I've attached our incident intake template to speed alignment. If we can get a MAP (mutual action plan) or short confirmation within 48 hours, that will allow us to notify stakeholders and satisfy our counsel's timing guidance. If preferable, we can jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Joanna Li
Security Operations Manager
Acme Health

Attachment: incident_template_acme.pdf (pdf)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Joanna Li <joanna.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — initial info request

Joanna — thanks for the heads-up and the template. Appreciate the clear asks.

On Tue, Sep 28, 2027 at 08:15 AM Joanna Li <joanna.li@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> We detected unusual activity that may have touched a small subset of user records...

Quick answers and a proposed next step: 

1) Acknowledgment window: Redwood's standard operational ack for inbound reports is 24 hours; for impacted-customer escalations we aim for a written acknowledgement inside 12 hours during business hours and a full operational readout within 48 hours. We can commit to initial ack inside 12 hours for priority incidents.

2) Export scope: We can produce a focused forensic snapshot limited to: timestamped request/response headers, request IDs, connection/session metadata, and user identifiers as hashed values (SHA-256 salted). We will redact full user content unless expressly requested and legally required. The redaction approach minimizes exposure while enabling triage.

3) Transfer method & custody: We prefer to transfer evidence over an encrypted SFTP endpoint provided by the customer (Acme-managed) or via an AWS S3 presigned URL to a bucket controlled by Acme. If a customer-managed endpoint is not available, Redwood can upload to a temporary, access-restricted storage we control and provide access logs; that may involve our infra subprocessor (for storage) depending on region.

4) Subprocessors: For exports originating from our US-hosted control plane + US compute, the likely subprocessors are our cloud storage provider and a licensed forensic vendor only if requested. We will not engage additional cross-border subprocessors for a limited export without explicit written consent. We'll provide a current subprocessor roster as an exhibit to the MAP.

Next step: I've attached a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft that captures the notice window (12h ack / 48h readout), export scope (identifiers hashed + metadata), transfer mechanics, and custody expectations. If that looks OK, sign and return or we can route via DocuSign.

Cc'ing Kim (privacy counsel) and Ben (forensics lead) to confirm operational constraints below.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_map_draft.docx (docx)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Joanna Li <joanna.li@acmehealth.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — initial info request

Joanna/Vanessa — one more operational note from the forensics team.

Operational process (high level):
- Snapshot creation: We take an immutable forensic snapshot at a specific UTC timestamp; snapshot includes request/response metadata and associated application logs for the time window you specify.
- Redaction: We run a redaction pass that strips payload/body content unless Acme requests a content-level export and signs a narrow SOW.
- Hashing: User identifiers will be hashed using a per-incident salt (we can provide the salt under an NDA or via an escrow mechanism if you require re-identification by mutual agreement).
- Chain of custody: Each snapshot is checksummed and logged; we provide a simple chain-of-custody manifest listing who accessed the artifact and when.
- Export methods: SFTP (customer endpoint) preferred; if using Redwood-hosted transfer, we will maintain logs and a time-limited presigned link. Transfer artifacts are encrypted in transit and at rest.

Potential limitations: If you require content-level artifacts or decrypted payloads, we will need written legal authorization and may require involvement of our forensic vendor (third party) depending on the compute environment. That will be an extra step and could add 72+ hours.

I've attached our export spec and a short SFTP checklist. If Acme can host an SFTP endpoint, we can begin snapshot generation immediately after the MAP is signed.

— Ben Carter
Senior Incident Response Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: forensics_export_specs.md (md), scp-instructions.txt (txt)
From: DataCounsel, LLP <contracts@datacounsel.example.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai; Joanna Li <joanna.li@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Limited forensic access & notice-window coordination for potential exposure

Vanessa / Joanna — thanks for the rapid coordination.

On Tue, Sep 28, 2027 at 03:20 PM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Joanna/Vanessa — one more operational note from the forensics team.

We represent Acme Health on privacy compliance. Our team reviewed the MAP draft and the export constraints Ben outlined. Acme can accept a hashed-identifier + metadata snapshot transferred to an Acme-controlled SFTP for immediate triage. Two small legal asks before we sign: 

1) Please include an explicit commitment in the MAP that Redwood will not persist a copy of the exported snapshot in any non-Redwood customer-controlled storage for more than 14 days post-transfer (other than existing platform logs retained per the DPA).
2) Provide the subprocessor roster exhibit (as Vanessa suggested) with the state of residence/hosting region for each subprocessed service used in the export path.

If you can accept those additions we will circulate a DocuSign link for signature by Acme and then provide SFTP details. We'll also provide an NDA addendum for the salt escrow if mutual re-identification is required during later stages.

Please confirm and, if accepted, route the final MAP via the DocuSign link below.

Regards,
Maya Turner
Partner, DataCounsel, LLP (on behalf of Acme Health)
